questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I've always wanted to go to Australia, and I thought that half a year (a semester) would be perfect to go, because it is so far away.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Australia is a really beautiful, easy and friendly country to be an exchange student in. Melbourne in particular is a very livable city and I had many good experiences and travels with other exchange students. The only downside about Melbourne is, that the weather in Melbourne is less predictable, than many other cities in Australia. Another thing to keep in mind, is that the living costs in Australia is pretty high, similar to Copenhagen.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Monash University was very good at giving information and had several instagrams with daily updates during the introduction week, as well as the rest of the semester.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I think that the social activites during the orientation week could have been better. I think it was also because of COVID, but the social gatherings were always outside/in a tent, which was too cold at that time.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I recommend joining every facebook page you can find with "renting in Melbourne" etc. The best page is "Fairy Floss", which is where me and my friend found our apartment. My recommendation is to be very active on the faccebook pages and update many times daily to see new posts. Write as soon as you see a post that could fit you. Also be openminded and even though the rental period they ask for does not match with yours completely then try and contact, because you never know. 

We lived in Richmond, which was a perfect area when you study at Monash, because it is right between CBD and the university. Try to find something close to the train-line that matches the one you take to Monash (e.g. we lived close to Richmond St. which was on the line to Caulfield and Clayton campus').

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
I would without doubt recommend living off-campus, as Monash University is very far away from Melbourne CBD. Areas like Fitzroy, Carlton, Collingwood, Richmond and CBD are nice areas to live in. As I did not have many courses with a lot of lectures, it was not that important to live close to the university. 

If you are expecting to be at university all day 5 days a week, maybe it would be best to live closer to campus. But then it is far to the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Off-campus: I was very satisfied, but also did a lot of work myself looking at facebook pages etc. But i know that many exchange students had to stay at student accomodations such as Scape, UniLodge etc. with very high rent.

On-campus: I have not heard anything or have any comments on the on-campus living.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Took a lot of time to look into courses, but the website made it as easy as one could ask for.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They had an online formula were the course codes etc. had to be filled out.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was useful to contact them via email.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Fine.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Follow the guidelines from Monash and contact them if you are in doubt.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic level was lower than at KU, but at the same time it was nice not to be too concerned with reading/assignments/exams. I learned a lot even though the level was lover. The professors varied a lot from course to course.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Easier than my BA courses at home.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Much more work were graded during the semester and counted as the final grade. Only one of my courses at Monash had a final exam (which only count for 50 % of the final grade). That is the biggest difference.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Economics of Climate Change, Climate Change Communication and Designing for Sustainability.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Economics of Climate Change and Climate Change Communication were courses that I can use for future references and especially Economics of Climate Change was interesting and a well composed course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Note that visa is around 3500 DKK and that flight tickets are expensive as well. I travelled a lot during the semester and after in campervans, which was more expensive (both rent of van and the overnights at camperspots.)  - but still worth it!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Coffee is cheap. Public transport is expensive if you are MA student, but as BA you get 50 % discount through Monash. Groceries are not cheap but it is the same as danish prices.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Monash had a lot to offer, but as I lived far away from campus, I did not sign up for anything.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would say everything, but I did not look into it a lot.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to the orientation week to meet people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
In Melbourne:  Go to nice cafes around Fitzroy, Collingwood etc. to study, play tennis, visit botanical garden, walk around the city, study at the state library in CBD, enjoy the sun while it is out because you never know i Melbourne.

Travel around Australia. Go to either Uluru or Cairns in the beginning (if you are going in the fall of Denmark), because Melbourne will be cold, but the north of Australia is warm. Go to Mornington Penninsula (close to Melbourne). See Great Ocean Road and visit Lorne as well as Torquay (nice surfing towns).Go to Byron Bay in mid-semester break. Visit Sydney. If you have the budget and time I would very much recommend visiting Tasmania, which is only 1,5 hours flight from MEL. Go in the summer time if possible. I can also recommend going to West Australia around south of Perth.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, people are very friendly and interested in Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just talk to them and invite them along if you are doing anything. They are very interested in learning about european countries.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Laid-back, friendly, day-by-day-mind set.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Try your best to find housing before leaving (unless you are going months before university starts).
2) Engage with other exchange students / local students in the beginning and make plans with people even though you dont really know them.
3) Don't expect to go to the beach everyday in Melbourne during fall semester (danish fall). The beaches around the city is not the best and the weather does not get very good until at least october/november. Bring warm clothes!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have in mind that Monash in not in the city, but outside. But the travel time does not feel long.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Insight in Australia's environmental and climate policies, new friendships and travels.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The time difference made it difficult to speak with friends/family at home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Spend a lot of time applying for grants, as it really pays off.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
